The kong vong (kong vong toch) is a traditional Khmer instrument made of sixteen gongs with raised centres hung on a circular rattan frame and struck with cloth-wrapped mallets. It is built much like the larger kong thom and belongs to the same family of traditional Khmer percussion, and it is often played with instruments such as the roneat. It is heard in Cambodian court music and traditional ensembles, and in pinpeat and mahaori orchestras. In its name, 'kong' refers broadly to a gong that is flat or has a raised centre, whether single or in a set.

Since the twentieth century, with deeper research into world music and a greater awareness of cultural preservation, the kong vong has been brought to international stages and has become an important representative of Southeast Asia's traditional musical culture.
